column6: Presents work they demonstrably own end to end (authored or drove it, responded to review, merged or delivered it); claims match the repo record when spot-checked. Explains what was and was not handed to AI tools, the checks that made that reasonable (tests, CI, review gates, staging, rollback), and the specific points where they stopped to validate, each with a reason tied to what was hard to reverse (schema, authentication, deployment, data migration, a data split or label definition, a save-file format). A delegation that went wrong counts as one of those points when they name the check it lacked and the check now in their sprint notes or repo record.
column9: Claims match the repo record, but the checks are named only in general terms ("we had tests"), no specific point where they stopped to validate is named with a reason tied to what was hard to reverse, or the reasons given for the delegation do not match the RFC, the decisions the team recorded, or the sprint notes. A delegation that went wrong, named with the check it lacked but with no new check in the record, scores here.
column12: Cannot say what they authored, reviewed, or merged in the work presented, gives no account of what was or was not handed to AI tools, describes delegating a hard-to-reverse change with no checks and no validation and cannot say what check it needed, or makes claims about what they authored, reviewed, or merged that contradict the repo record.
column15: Unexcused no-show, or no meaningful attempt to present or answer; excused absences are rescheduled per the absence policy and not scored here.

column2: Judgment: why this approach, what was rejected, what was hard to reverse [SO1]
column6: Explains why this approach was chosen, names at least two alternatives that were considered (doing nothing counts as one), each with the reason it was rejected, consistent with the RFC, the decisions the team recorded, or the sprint notes where they cover it, and identifies which parts of the decision were hard to reverse.
column9: Explains the chosen approach, but names only one alternative, names alternatives without the reason each was rejected, gives alternatives or reasons that do not match the RFC, the decisions the team recorded, or the sprint notes, or cannot say which parts were hard to reverse.
column12: Cannot explain why the work was done this way, or names no alternative that was considered.
column15: Unexcused no-show, or no meaningful attempt to present or answer; excused absences are rescheduled per the absence policy and not scored here.

column6: Answers "what breaks if X changes" questions with correct, specific reasoning about the system's behavior and limits, including where they chose to verify the system's behavior themselves rather than rely on generated output.
column9: Answers are mostly correct but do not name the specific behavior or limit that breaks, reasoning falters on follow-up questions, or the student names no point where they verified the system's behavior themselves.
column12: Answers are incorrect or evasive, or cannot say what the system does when X changes.
column15: Unexcused no-show, or no meaningful attempt to present or answer; excused absences are rescheduled per the absence policy and not scored here.

column2: Role, team accountability, and work distribution [SO5]
column6: Articulates what their named role (PM, AI Coordinator, Quality Owner) or comparable ownership area required this term, with concrete examples; names a decision they chaired to a conclusion this term that matches the sprint-note record, or, where their turn to chair is still ahead, the decision the charter's rotation schedules them to chair and when; and explains how the team's decisions actually got made and how work was distributed.
column9: Describes the role and team process in general terms, with few concrete examples of what the role required in practice or of how work was distributed, or names no decision they chaired or are scheduled to chair.
column12: Cannot articulate what their role or ownership area required, how the team makes decisions, or who did what.
column15: Unexcused no-show, or no meaningful attempt to present or answer; excused absences are rescheduled per the absence policy and not scored here.

column6: Answers the question asked, at a level of detail the assessor does not have to correct; at the edge of their knowledge, says "I don't know, but here is how I would find out" (that scores; bluffing does not). Names a specific thing they told someone whose work they reviewed, and what changed in that work because of it, or what they checked and why it needed no change; in fall and winter, where the reviewed RFC is not revised yet, the author's response to the comment (the reply, or the revision the author committed to) counts as what changed.
column9: Answers, but the assessor has to ask for a more concrete or a shorter answer, or hesitates at the edge of their knowledge without saying how they would find out. Names a real review comment but cannot say what changed.
column12: Does not answer the question asked, or bluffs instead of saying what they do not know. Cannot name anything they told a reviewee, or offers feedback that named nothing specific and requested no change.
column15: Unexcused no-show, or no meaningful attempt to present or answer; excused absences are rescheduled per the absence policy and not scored here.
